QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_12

question.text: A Social Impact Fund launched EXCLUSIVELY for investment in securities of NPOs registered or listed on a Social Stock Exchange may invest what percentage of its investable funds in such NPO securities?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Section 2.3.1.3, a Social Impact Fund (or scheme of a SIF) launched EXCLUSIVELY for registered or listed NPOs may invest up to 100% of its investable funds in securities of NPOs on an SSE. A non-exclusive, existing SIF is capped at 25%. The 75% figure in Section 2.3.2.1 applies to SIFs issued by AIFs investing in unlisted securities/partnership interests of social ventures / SE securities — a different rule. **The Trap:** 25% is the existing-fund cap (not exclusive). 51% is an irrelevant 'control' threshold. 75% confuses with the FPE-side SIF rule (75% in SV/SE securities). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A/B/C/D/E treat AIF investment conditions; the 25% / 75% / 100% distinctions are classic traps also relevant to XV (RA) valuing listed Section 8 FPEs. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When your NPO client is the investee of a SIF, review the SIF's PPM (Private Placement Memorandum) to confirm whether it is the 'exclusive-for-NPOs' type (100% allowed) or the existing-SIF type (25% cap) — this affects sampling: for exclusive-SIF funded programs you can assume near-full attribution to SSE-listed NPOs.
